case_name: Dalip Singh v State of Punjab
respondent:
State of Punjab
Supreme Court of India

8 July 1997
Cr.A. No. 188 of 1985
The Judgment was delivered by: M. K. Mukherjee, J.
1. Dalip Singh the appellant before us and five
facts: Dalip Singh and five others were tried by a Special Court for rioting, murder, and other related offenses.
The trial ended in conviction of Dalip Singh and others under various IPC sections.
Only Dalip Singh appealed to the Supreme Court.
The case involved a dispute over a water outlet on a field.
Mohinder Singh died as a result of injuries sustained by him.
Shabeg Singh, Bagicha Singh, and Rachhpal Singh were injured during the incident.
issues: Whether the incident took place in the manner alleged by the prosecution or the defense?
Whether the evidence presented was legally admissible?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution relied on the testimonies of Shabeg Singh (P.W.6) and Bagicha Singh (P.W 7).
Dalip Singh gave two gandasa blows to Mohinder Singh, who fell down.
Bagicha Singh tried to intervene and both Shabeg Singh and Rachhpal Singh gave takwa blows on him with their takwas.
respondent_arguments: The defense claimed that the incident did not occur as alleged by the prosecution.
The accused were not present at the scene of the incident.
The outlet was near the place where Mohinder Singh was injured.
court_reasoning: The court found that the undisputed facts showed that Mohinder Singh died as a result of injuries sustained by him, and Shabeg Singh, Bagicha Singh, and Rachhpal Singh were injured during the incident.
The court rejected the defense's claim that the accused were not present at the scene of the incident.
The court held that the evidence presented was not legally admissible.
holding: The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of Dalip Singh and others under various IPC sections.
The court rejected the appeal and affirmed the impugned order of conviction and sentence.
